1,796 cc [[Nissan CA engine#CA18(i)|''CA18, CA18S'']] I4 | transmission = 5-speed manual
3-speed automatic | weight = {{convert|1050|-|1070|kg|lb|abbr=on}} | body_style = 5-door [[notchback]]
5-door [[fastback]] |predecessor = [[Datsun 510|Yue Loong 706]] |class = [[Compact car]] ([[C-segment|C]]) | related = [[Nissan Stanza#T12 series (1986–1990)|Nissan Auster/Stanza]] | aka = Yulon Arex | designer = }} The '''Yue Loong Feeling''' ({{zh|c=裕隆飛羚|p=Yùlóng Fēilíng}}) 101/102 is a [[compact car]] built in [[Taiwan]] by the [[Yulon|Yue Loong Motor Company]] from 1986 until 1995.{{cite web | title = 飛羚的銷售數字 | trans-title = Yue Loong Feeling 101/102 & Arex 601 Production volume by year | url = http://tw.myblog.yahoo.com/ytseng3ford/article?mid=28128&prev=29988&next=28127&l=f&fid=25 | work = tw.myblog.yahoo.com/ytseng3ford/ | publisher = ytseng3ford | date = 2008-10-06 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120321224258/http://tw.myblog.yahoo.com/ytseng3ford/article?mid=28128&prev=29988&next=28127&l=f&fid=25 | archive-date = 2012-03-21 }}{{cite web | title = Het mysterie Yue Loong |trans-title=The Yue Loong Mystery | language = nl | url = http://www.autoweek.nl/forum/read.php?6,3902757 | work = AutoWeek.nl | publisher = Sanoma Men's Magazines B.V | date = 2009-01-30 }} It is available in both five-door notchback and five-door fastback body styles. ==History== First presented on 25 October 1986, it was heavily based on the [[Nissan Stanza#T11|'''T11''' Auster/Stanza]], built by [[Yulon]]'s principal associated company and engineering partner [[Nissan]]. Despite Yulon having invested heavily in a new R&D center (in Guishan) and having spent five years in development,{{Cite web |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20101124033023/http://www.yulon-motor.com.tw/company_e/history.asp |title = Company History |url = http://www.yulon-motor.com.tw/company_e/history.asp |publisher = Yulon Motor |archive-date = 2010-11-24 |url-status = dead }} hiring 300 technicians and spending NT $2 billion in the process, the car failed in the marketplace due to much publicized quality concerns. The Feeling was also marketed abroad (even in Europe), unusual for Taiwanese built cars. After a disappointing 9,451 built in the first full year, production dropped to a mere 3,846 the second year (1988).{{Cite book | last = Chen | first = Chia-wen | title = An Economic Analysis of Taiwan's Automobile Industry | publisher = MIT | year = 1995 | page = 93 | location = Cambridge, MA | url = http://dspace.mit.edu/bitstream/handle/1721.1/37548/33817380.pdf | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120314013952/http://dspace.mit.edu/bitstream/handle/1721.1/37548/33817380.pdf | archive-date = 2012-03-14 }} The Feeling was even displayed at the 1987 [[Tokyo Motor Show]].{{cite web | title = 日本CG1980年代車系專書所收錄的飛羚101 | trans-title = Japanese CG 1980's include Feeling 101 | date = 2008-08-15 | url = http://tw.myblog.yahoo.com/ytseng3ford/article?mid=22794&next=22549&l=f&fid=25 | publisher = Bikers Street Beat | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120321223324/http://tw.myblog.yahoo.com/ytseng3ford/article?mid=22794&next=22549&l=f&fid=25 | archive-date = 2012-03-21 }} [[File:Yue Loong Feeling 1.8GTX FP-BV-92 20141101f.jpg|thumb|left|The front of the only Yue Loong Feeling that remains in Europe]] The Feeling was recognizable by its unusual three-piece, wrap around rear window. A 1.6 or a 1.8-litre four cylinder [[Nissan CA engine|Nissan CA]] gasoline engine was available, with {{cvt|88|or|97|hp-metric|kW|0}}. The 1.6 was added during 1987, complementing the pricier 1.8. Top speeds were {{convert|160|and|170|km/h|mph|0|abbr=on}} respectively.{{cite book | title = BilKatalogen 1989 ''(Swedish edition of German'' Auto Katalog'')'' | language = sv | editor = Dackevall, Gunnar | publisher = PM Press AB | location = Stockholm, Sweden | page = 102 | id = 0284-365X | year = 1988 }} The bigger engine's bore was 0.3 mm less than its 1809 cc Nissan counterpart, so as to squeeze beneath Taiwan's 1.8-litre tax threshold. The facelifted '''Feeling 102''' was released in June 1989,{{citation | title = Yue Loong Motor Co. Ltd. ''(catalog)'' | language = zh, en | url = http://storm.oldcarmanualproject.com/yulon/Yulon%20intorduction%201415.jpg | publisher = Yue Loong Motor Company | page = 13 | year = 1990 | access-date = 2011-03-04 }} when claimed top speeds increased to 180 and 185 km/h for the 1.6 and 1.8 (190 km/h in the notchback 1.8).{{Cite book| title = Quattroruote: Tutte le Auto del Mondo 1992 | publisher = Editoriale Domus | year = 1992 | pages = 1184–1186 | location = Milano }} The Feeling was imported to the Netherlands by the Abemy Group in [[Sassenheim]] during 1992. Brought over in three models (1.6 LS, 1.8 LSX, 1.8 GTX) it failed to make a splash in the marketplace. Only 122 were sold in 1992, with a total of 130 brought in. All examples were then bought back by the importer who was unable to supply spare parts for the cars. Later it was discovered that one car is still in the Netherlands, in a private collection. Yue Loong's attempt at breaking into the European market was over. [[File:Yue Loong Feeling 1.8GTX FP-BV-92 20141101e.jpg|thumb|left|Rear end]] [[File:1992 Yue Loong Feeling dashboard.jpg|thumb|right|Dashboard]] {{anchor|Arex}} ==Yulon Arex== [[File:1994 Yulon Arex GLi 1800cc manual transmission right-back.jpg|thumb|left|1994 Yulon Arex 1.8 GLi (5-door)]] The 102 was replaced by the '''Yulon 601 Arex''' ({{zh|裕隆精兵}}) 1.8i in summer 1993, by which time the company had switched the romanized version of their name to become "Yulon".{{cite book | title = Automobil Revue 1994 | editor-last = Büschi | editor-first = Hans-Ulrich | publisher = Hallwag AG | location = Berne, Switzerland | language = de, fr | page = 581 | volume = 89 |date=10 March 1994 | isbn = 3-444-00584-9 }} The Arex featured a newly designed front with flip-up headlights and blistered fenders, as well as a Lucas fuel injection system which increases power to {{convert|103|PS|kW|0|abbr=on}} at 5,300 rpm. Top speed remained around {{convert|185|km/h|mph|0|abbr=on}}, depending on bodystyle and transmission. After no more than 4,300 were made, Yulon halted their attempts at making a Taiwanese national car in 1995. extract: The Yue Loong Feeling (Chinese: 裕隆飛羚; pinyin: Yùlóng Fēilíng) 101/102 is a compact car built in Taiwan by the Yue Loong Motor Company from 1986 until 1995. It is available in both five-door notchback and five-door fastback body styles.
